title: Herbivory and natural selection on flowering phenology in wild sunflower Helianthus annuus
screening_reason: Seasonal abundance/damage of five seed-feeding herbivores and plant fitness were measured in the same population; damage by Homoeosoma and Suleima explains apparent selection for later flowering. Numeric synchrony-to-fitness effect plus variance still needs source-level recovery.
notes: Highest-priority new strict-antagonist candidate. Damage by three enemies declines through flowering season; one increases and seed weevils are constant. Do not substitute mediated-selection conclusion for a common H1 effect.

title: Individual flowering schedule fruit set and flower and seed predation in Vaccinium hirtum Thunb. (Ericaceae)
screening_reason: Individual flowering rank/synchrony, fruit set, hand-pollination response and multiple flower/seed predator attacks were measured for four subpopulations over two years, but independent pollinator/predator activity curves are not the common exposure.
notes: Kyoto system. Early plants show pollinator limitation while later plants can suffer more weevil/fly attack; conspecific flowering synchrony itself did not correlate with fruit set or predation. Excellent counterselection context.

title: Impact of plant flowering phenology on the cost benefit balance in a nursery pollination mutualism with honest males and cheating females
screening_reason: Host flowering phenology and pollinator emergence were directly monitored and female fruit production was pollen/pollinator limited, but costs and benefits are sex-specific: larvae develop in male inflorescences while female fruit success is measured separately.
notes: Chamaerops humilis × Derelomus chamaeropsis. Strong timing/mutualism lead, but no single individual-level net mixed fitness scale.

title: Comparative impacts of long-term trends in snowmelt and species interactions on plant population dynamics
screening_reason: Thirteen flowering seasons of pollen-limitation and seed-predation experiments plus long-term demography directly quantify both biotic effects on seed production, but the focal exposure is snowmelt/year rather than plant-partner phenological overlap.
notes: Ipomopsis aggregata. Valuable matched benefit/cost architecture and long-term negative/null evidence: neither pollen limitation nor seed predation changed detectably with snowmelt date.

title: Increased pre-dispersal seed predation in sunflower crop-wild hybrids
screening_reason: Flowering date strongly predicts seed-predator damage and few wild plants flower at peak damage times, but insect activity is inferred mainly from damage timing and final fitness is handled in linked papers rather than as one direct synchrony effect.
notes: Helianthus annuus crop-wild experiment; use with linked 2002 fecundity paper only under explicit dependence mapping.

title: Effects of flower and seed predators and pollinators on fruit production in two sequentially flowering congeners
screening_reason: Sequentially flowering Vaccinium congeners were compared with pollinator limitation and flower/seed predation, but multiple agents and species differences prevent one partner-synchrony H1 effect.
notes: Mahoro 2003; backward-search companion to IWE036. Useful for evidence-architecture synthesis.
